title: Governing principles
summary: The owner's rules that settle design questions everywhere in the app.
description: These come from the app's owner and change only on their word. When a change is unclear, or two parts of the app disagree, these decide. Each is stated here as something that can be checked; the parts of the spec that carry them out refer back.

requirements.text: A course is made for what the learner asks for; the app never decides what is worth learning.
A level (CEFR, A1 to C2) describes material and never limits what can be made or practised: a request at any level is made as asked.
Nothing the tutor makes waits for approval: keeping it is approving it, deleting it is rejecting it.

The app does not fill in the learner's existing content by itself at startup. When a new feature needs something existing content lacks, a button asks the tutor to add it, in a conversation the learner can read.
A course can be finished regardless of time: passing a lesson again the same day always adds mastery points, and no step toward mastery requires waiting for a check-in to come due.
Mastery is never lost through practice: a mastered lesson stays mastered whatever its later results. Only the learner's own reset of progress clears it.
Closing a mastered course is final: nothing is added to it, changed in it or brought back from it.
A mastered subject is revisited through a new course from the tutor, never by reopening the old one.
The day's list is a short way in, not a backlog: what is due never piles up on the home screen.
A lesson that fits no course goes in the single folder Other lessons.
For each song and podcast, enough is kept to rebuild the exact prompt that made it.
A lesson type is declared in one place, and the screens and the lesson flow ask the type instead of branching on it.
Every row that names a thing (a course, a lesson, a word, a song, a memory) has a tagged id that says what it is; screens show the title of the thing instead of the id.

questions: Speech stored as WAV by earlier versions is re-encoded to MP3 by itself at startup, with no button. Is that storage housekeeping, which PRIN-4 allows, or a change to the learner's content that should wait for the learner to ask?

Three more things change existing content at startup without being asked: lessons built on Wikipedia are corrected by an AI every 90 days (a paid request), unchanged courses from the old built-in collection are removed, and courses mastered under earlier rules are moved to mastered. Are these the ongoing work PRIN-4 allows?

PRIN-12 holds for the screens, but the core still names lesson types outside the registry: in statistics (dialogue, writing and listening counts), in a few tutor tools, and when a course's items are cut into drills. Should those move into the types?
Reset progress clears mastery on every lesson, including the lessons of closed courses, while the courses stay closed. Is a closed course with unmastered lessons intended?
